newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chechen rebel commander frees Russian policemen. [corrected 20 36 gmt]
newsitem.headline: Chechen rebel commander frees Russian policemen. [corrected 20 36 gmt]

text.p: Chechen rebel field commander Salman Raduyev on Wednesday released a group of Russian policemen whose capture four days ago threw a shadow over the breakaway region's fragile peace process.

Interior ministry spokesman Vladimir Vorozhtsov said the policemen, 21 Russians and one from the Dagestan region bordering Chechnya, were handed over at 3.30 pm (1230 GMT) in the settlement of Gerzel-Kutan.
"There had been pressure on Raduyev from all sides, from both Chechen and Russian officials, to free the policemen," Vorozhtsov told Reuters.
He said senior Kremlin official Boris Berezovsky, who has been visiting Chechnya this week, had also used his influence to persuade Raduyev to release the captives.
Russian television said Berezovsky had offered to release 11 Chechens held captive by the Russian side in return for the policemen. This report could not be immediately confirmed.

Raduyev, who led a bloody hostage-taking raid in Dagestan last January (corrects from "the southern Russian city of Budennovsk last year"), seized the policemen after they refused to allow his men to enter Dagestan.
He said on Tuesday he wanted Russia to apologise for not letting him into Dagestan and could kill his hostages if anyone tried to free them by force.

The separatist leadership in Chechnya, keen not to derail the peace process and threaten local elections scheduled for January 27, had promised to force Raduyev to release all his hostages unconditionally.
Moscow had indicated the incident might delay the withdrawal of its troops from Chechnya as arranged under a peace deal it signed with the separatists last August.

The slaying of six foreign aid workers in Chechnya on Tuesday has also highlighted the tension in a region still devastated by 21 months of fierce fighting between Russian troops and the rebels, who are seeking Chechen independence.
